result.topic_en: Latin notes on the heat-conduction prize problem: for the case n = 2, the equation II splits into two equations independent of the third variable, Δu = 0 and Λu = ∂u/∂t; normal forms for Δ are listed, and ΔΛu = 0 is derived, leading to two cases depending on whether this follows from Δu = 0.
result.transcription:
in hoc casu semper a $\gamma$ independentem manere,
si temperatura initialis sit functio quaelibet
solarum $\alpha$ et $\beta$.

Casus secundus, $n=2$

Si aequatio II in duas aequationes a $\gamma$
independentes discinditur, ope alterius $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
ex altera ejici potest. Brevitatis causa haec
ita exhibeatur
$(1)\quad \Delta u = 0$
illa
$(2)\quad \Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
denotantibus $\Delta$ et $\Lambda$ expressiones characteristicas ex $\partial_\alpha$ et $\partial_\beta$ conflatas.

Aequationem priorem facile perspicitur mutatis variabilibus independentibus ita transformari posse ut sit $\Delta$
vel $= \partial_\alpha\partial_\beta + e\,\partial_\alpha + f\,\partial_\beta$
vel $= \partial_\alpha^2 + e\,\partial_\alpha + f\,\partial_\beta$
vel $= \partial_\alpha$
valoribus $e=0$ $f=0$ non exclusis.

Quoniam sit
$0 = \partial_t \Delta u = \Delta \partial_t u = \Delta\Lambda u$
ex his duabus aequationibus (1) [-et-] et (2)
sequitur:
$(3)\quad \Delta\Lambda u = 0$
Jam duo distinguendi sunt casus, prout
haec aequatio (3) vel ex aequatione (1) fluat ($\alpha$)
sive sit
$\Delta\Lambda = \Theta\Delta$
denotante $\Theta$ novam expressionem characteristicam, vel non fluat ($\beta$) novamque aequationem a $\Delta u$ independentem sistat.

Casum priorem ($\alpha$) ut saltem pro una forma ipsius $\Delta$ persecutemur, supponamus
$\Delta = \partial_\alpha\partial_\beta + e\,\partial_\alpha + f\,\partial_\beta$.
Tum $\Delta\Lambda u$ ope aequationis $\Delta u = 0$ ad expressionem

methods.what: Splitting equation II into a time-independent constraint and an evolution equation (elimination of ∂u/∂t)
Normal forms of a second-order operator in two variables under change of independent variables
methods.quote:

Case distinction: the compatibility condition follows from Δu=0 iff the operator factorization ΔΛ = ΘΔ holds

items.quote:
in hoc casu semper a $\gamma$ independentem manere,
si temperatura initialis sit functio quaelibet
solarum $\alpha$ et $\beta$.
items.english: in this case [the temperature] always remains independent of γ, if the initial temperature is any function of α and β alone.

items.quote: Aequationem priorem facile perspicitur mutatis variabilibus independentibus ita transformari posse ut sit $\Delta$
items.english: It is easily seen that the former equation can be transformed, by changing the independent variables, so that Δ is one of the following forms.

items.quote:
Casum priorem ($\alpha$) ut saltem pro una forma ipsius $\Delta$ persecutemur, supponamus
$\Delta = \partial_\alpha\partial_\beta + e\,\partial_\alpha + f\,\partial_\beta$.
items.english: In order to pursue the first case (α) at least for one form of Δ, let us suppose Δ = ∂α∂β + e∂α + f∂β.
